item.title: Jeff Pearlman puts Stephen A. Smith on notice after controversial Lakers comments
item.description: Credit: Jeff Pearlman on TikTok, Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Stephen A. Smith expressed confidence that he could one day become President of the United States, stating that he felt like he belonged at the White House after staging a lackluster interview with President Donald Trump there last week. Jeff Pearlman isn’t buying Smith’s bravado. On Thursday, Pearlman, a longtime sports journalist and New York Times bestselling author, posted a TikTok captioned, “Stephen A. Smith’s take on the Lakers is telling of his decline from relevancy.” Oh, that’s right. All that Trump talk , I totally forgot that Smith can’t stop doubling and tripling down on the take that the scorching-hot Los Angeles Lakers cannot win the NBA title because Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler are all “ white dudes .” Back to Pearlman. “Sometimes, you make the mistake of scrolling the internet,” Pearlman said in his TikTok. “And this is what Stephen A. Smith said about the Lakers possibly winning a championship. This is a direct quote: ‘I’m looking at the brothers, and I’m saying, L.A. doing special things. These white brothers can play. Y’all gonna let them win a championship?’ And I— we are witnessing a career dissolve in front of us.” “I actually mean that,” Pearlman continued. “He doesn’t see it yet, but I 100 percent do. We are witnessing a career dissolve in front of us. And what you are seeing right now is Stephen A. Smith, the backlash to his Trump interview , insane. The most backlash he’s taken in a long time because he did a sh*tty job. Then, instead of acknowledging he does a sh*tty job, he doubles down. “Then, to distract from the sh*tty job he did, he does a really stupid take, which, of course, he does a lot of. But a really stupid take.” Pearlman repeated Smith’s line and observed that the chaotic aftermath of that take “distracts from the original inanity and awfulness of his Trump interview.” “I feel like it’s all by design,” Pearlman said. “I actually do think we’re watching a guy dissolve. And I was kind of wondering if the Pat McAfee rise and the Stephen A. Smith fall are related in any way, where it’s hard to watch someone take what was yours. And then you’re grabbing, grabbing, grabbing. You’re reaching, and you’re reaching, and you’re trying to maintain what you don’t have anymore. And one day, you look up, and you’re like, ‘Oh, I’m forgotten.’ “I do want to say, sports history is littered — in fact, media history is littered — with people like Stephen A. Smith. People whose substance lags far behind their performative nature. Rush Limbaugh, perfect example. Who even remembers Rush Limbaugh anymore? I know he died. I’m just saying, the cemeteries are filled with irreplaceable men.” Well, that took a turn. But Pearlman’s general point has merit, even if Smith is more ubiquitous than ever right now. item.title: Alcaraz puts injury concerns aside to take apart Cobolli
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz has never won the season-ending ATP Finals title [Getty Images] A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz put aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages. Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday. He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win. The six-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory. "I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said. "I'm just really happy that I am getting more confident, the way I'm hitting the ball and seeing what's going on in the match. "The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow." Alcaraz is now on a 12-match winning streak and will face Ben Shelton, who he beat in the Paris Masters final last month, in Saturday's semi-finals. The winner of Friday's last match between Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe will face Alexander Zverev in the other semi-final. Alcaraz was conservative in his movement, trying to avoid sliding in and out of the corners - but rather than diminishing his game, it allowed him to produce some astonishing shot-making. Cobolli never looked as though he had the belief that he could challenge Alcaraz, and was broken in the first game of the match by a thumping return winner. Alcaraz kept the points short, hammering his forehand and backhand to all corners, and targeted Cobolli's second serve in particular. An astonishing whipped 110mph forehand winner was the highlight of the first set, which Alcaraz wrapped up with a strong service hold. Cobolli again lost his serve in the opening game of the second set and Alcaraz claimed five of the final six games to secure victory. After converting match point with another return winner, Alcaraz embraced Cobolli at the net and offered the crushed Italian a few words of support. Alcaraz has not had his serve broken once in his three group matches as he bids for a first title at the season-ending event. He and world number one Zverev have both made it through the group stages without dropping a set, while Alcaraz has not lost more than four games in a set. In the doubles, Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison reached the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 victory over Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos. The US Open champions will face fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic for a place in Sunday's final. There was a flurry of activity this week, beginning with Tuesday afternoon’s deadline to protect players from the 2026 Rule 5 Draft. Free-agent right-handed pitchers Sonny Gray and Dustin May signed new contracts with the Minnesota Twins and Chicago White Sox, respectively. Additionally, two major trades took place. On Wednesday, the Seattle Mariners sent right-handed pitcher Bryce Miller and two other pitchers to the Kansas City Royals in exchange for third baseman Maikel Garcia and two pitchers. On Thursday, the Colorado Rockies acquired right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo from the Chicago White Sox in exchange for two minor league players. Some players will likely wait until a new labor agreement is reached before deciding on their next career moves. Execs and agents reporting that there are a ton of conversations happening, and the top layer of free agents will get deals. The matchup will also serve as Florida State’s Seminole Heritage Game, honoring the Seminole Tribe of Florida, and the team will wear its turquoise uniforms. item.title: Siena men's basketball turns page to Bucknell after historic 47-point loss at St. John's
item.description: St. John's Tounde Yessoufou (24) knocks the ball away from Siena's Parrish Edmond Jr. (3) during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in the Queens borough of New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) (Frank Franklin II/Associated Press) Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith was ready to put one of the most lopsided losses in program history in the rearview mirror even before boarding the team bus outside Carnesecca Arena on Wednesday night. The Saints lost 119-72 to No. 13 St. John's in Queens, a 47-point margin of defeat that tied for the third-largest in 89 seasons of Siena basketball. "Definitely stuff to build on, but not one we're going to worry about or talk about much," Smith said. "We're just moving on and trying to get a win on Saturday (at Bucknell)." Smith said he believed his young players wouldn't overreact to the loss, which came against the defending Big East Conference Tournament champions, led by Hall of Fame coach Rick Pitino. "They know that was the best team we're going to play," Smith said. "I think it can roll off their back. I can try to instill the fact that you lose by 1, you lose by 60, it doesn't matter." Siena's only two bigger blowouts came at Syracuse. The Saints lost there by 52 points (144-92) to the 12th-ranked Orange on Jan. 17, 1979 and by 51 (123-72) to No. 7 Syracuse on Jan. 2, 1988. Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa, who had a team-high 16 points Wednesday, was ready to turn the page to Bucknell. "It's kind of the life of college basketball," he said. "You lose a game, you've got to play the next one. Just keep your head up and on to the next, I guess." Smith said it's easy for the score to get out of hand given that Siena (3-2) plays at one of the fastest paces in the country, which didn't faze a St. John's team that loves to press and run. "Score doesn't matter," he said. "The pace we play, you can never look at how many points we give up or even how many points we score. It doesn't matter. Are we efficient with our shots? Do we take the right ones. Are we getting a good point-per-shot?" Smith said Siena didn't do any of the three things he emphasized before the game: avoiding turnovers in live play, grabbing defensive rebounds and making shots. The Saints committed 15 turnovers that led to 29 St. John's points. The Red Storm had 16 offensive rebounds for 20 second-chance points. Siena shot 35.1% from the field and again struggled from 3-point range, shooting 9-for-35. "The third one, you can't really control," Smith said. "The first two we had more control over, and we didn't do a great job. Understand that's what we needed to do and we didn't do it." St. John surged to an 18-2 lead. However, the Red Storm only outscored Siena 39-38 the rest of the half to take a 57-40 lead into halftime. item.title: Throwback Dawg Day: Lambert, Georgia Hang 50-Plus On The HBC
item.description: September 19, 2015: Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Greyson Lambert (11) reacts after a touchdown in first half action of the South Carolina Gamecocks at Georgia Bulldogs game at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Have you ever had a moment of, ‘ok where in the world did that come from?’ If you were in Sanford Stadium the night of Sept, 20, 2015, you certainly experienced it. To say that the expectations for Greyson Lambert upon his transfer to Georgia from Virginia were cautious would be accurate. After all, how good could someone be who went elsewhere due to not winning a starting job at an ACC also-ran? And when you have outings like Lambert had in mid-September by going 11-21 passing against Vanderbilt, the common thinking was that he was in a role to support a very good running game, but not someone who could take over a game. That whole thinking sailed into the vapor and whisked itself up Baxter Hill on this night against South Carolina, when Lambert not only set an NCAA record on a 96 percent completion percentage, but his 24-of-25 night also set a Georgia record for most completed passes in a row. It all stacked up to Georgia rolling up 576 yards in a 52-20 win. And those 52 points were gratifying due to one opposing adversary: Steve Spurrier. The Head Ball Coach famously broke 50 points against Georgia in Athens and bragged about it. Not only that, but his return to college coaching at South Carolina further twisted the knife in Georgia’s back, misery worsened in a three-game losing streak against the Dawgs from 2010 to 2012. On this night, however, it was Georgia pouring it on to the tune of 576 yards. The big showing was not just Lambert. When you have a stable of running backs including two of the best in school history, the job has a degree of ease. Nick Chubb and Sony Michel each had touchdown runs in the second quarter before a five-yard toss to Malcolm Mitchell capped a 21-point second quarter after the game started 3-3. Michel got into the passing game act in the second half with two touchdowns receptions ahead of scoring runs by Chubb and Keith Marshall. Now, Georgia fans cannot officially claim this loss compelled Coach Spurrier to retire the next month after USC slumped to a 2-4 overall start. But it’s a fun assumption to claim. Go Dawgs!

With two games to go, who knows what sort of misery is in store?? The latest antagonist will be the sport’s newest darling: the undefeated UCLA Bruins and Bob Chesney. Even after losing Nico Iamaleava, the Bruins just keep winning, having a great shot at the Big Ten Championship Game (again: RIP) and will surely make their College Football Playoff debut. However, despite a 10-0 record, UCLA sits just fourth in the rankings behind multiple teams with losses, perhaps due to less favorable analytics. For example, SP+ has this team 12th nationally, which is still very strong — and certainly much higher than Michigan at No. 43, which corresponds to an 11.5-point gap between these teams. That is not how Vegas sees things, though, which bafflingly has UCLA favored by essentially a field goal. Nothing is ever off the table, and this game is being played in Ann Arbor, but a lot has to improve for the Wolverines to actually pull off the upset. Unfortunate timing to finally get UCLA three years into expansion when the program is somehow having a historic season, but this Michigan team might have trouble against anyone right now, so oh well. Offense: Fool me 10 times… Everyone already knows the stats, and anyone who has watched even five minutes of the Michigan offense this season knows just how bleak things are on this side of the ball. The Argentinian is still with the United States national team at present, concluding a two-legged CONCACAF Nations League meeting with Haiti – the first game of which was last night – and is due to start work with the Reds on 18 November. item.description: ATLANTA - DECEMBER 8: Quarterback Matt Mauck #18 of the LSU Tigers falls forward during the Southeastern Conference Championship Game against the Tennessee Volunteers on December 8, 2001 at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Georgia. In some ways, it is similar to the history between LSU and Tennessee. If you have not read or seen any of the series, the brief on the story is: in a dystopian nation, the government selects one boy and one girl between the ages of 12 and 18 as tributes from each of the country’s 12 districts to enter an arena where “Gamemakers” change certain aspects of the arena while the tributes fight to the death until only one remains. The other tributes typically are not the scariest part of the arena. It is the Gamemakers sitting in a control room, randomly changing the weather, releasing bioengineered animals, supplying barbaric weaponry, and breaking your expectations the second things start looking predictable. This is what some of the Tigers’ and Volunteers’ most iconic moments together have felt like: an invisible control room hijacking the battle and rewriting expectations. LSU and Tennessee first met in 1925 in Knoxville, Tennessee, where they battled to a 0-0 tie. Since then, the Vols have held the series bragging rights with a 21-10-3 record. Tennessee strung together 10 consecutive victories from 1934 to 1959. It was almost 13, but a 3-3 tie in 1964 broke up the win streak. Since the turn of the century, LSU has dominated the series, leading 7-3 in that timeframe. “The Stop” in 1959 marked one of the most iconic moments in the history of this matchup’s early years. item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 25: Wade Davis #71 of the Colorado Rockies pitches during a baseball game against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on July 25, 2019 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dating back to 1871, over 23,000 people have played Major League Baseball. Of those, 281 players have been granted admission to the Baseball Hall of Fame (354 total people, including managers, pioneers, executives and umpires). It’s an elite group that includes Rockies legends Larry Walker and Todd Helton , who both were honored with statues outside of Coors Field this season. Jim Leyland, who managed the Rockies in 2024, was also elected in 2024 with Helton. The next likely candidate with a chance to get 75% of the vote is eight-time All-Star Nolan Arenado, but it will be five years after his playing days end before he is eligible. But there’s another former Rockie on this year’s ballot who deserves some praise. Wade Davis, a three-time All-Star reliever, was a member of the “super bullpen” the Rockies brought in before the 2018 season. The infamous trio didn’t live up to its billing, but Davis still had a tremendous career that’s worth recognizing. Earlier this week, Davis was named as one of 14 new players added to the ballot for the HOF class of 2027. The list is highlighted by catcher Buster Posey and pitcher Jon Lestor, but doesn’t include any runaway first-ballot inductees. They will join 13 holdovers from previous years, including Chase Utley, who earned 59.1% of the vote last year. Although he was eligible, former Rockie outfielder Dexter Fowler was left off the ballot. He’s certainly worth an honorable mention here, as he was a fan favorite, and he remains the Rockies single-season leader in triples (15 in 2011). Journeyman catcher Jonathan Lucroy, who played with the Rockies in 2017, had a distinguished 12-year career with nine teams, but also didn’t make the cut, despite being eligible. The Baseball Writers’ Association of America will fill out their ballots between now and Dec. 31, and the results will be announced on Jan. 19. The Hall of Fame Induction Weekend is slated for July 23-26. As for Davis, he was a shutdown pitcher from 2009-2017. With four years on the Tampa Bay Rays, four more with the Kansas City Royals, and another with the Chicago Cubs, the righty posted a 12.2 rWAR. In 393 appearances, including 88 starts, he posted a 3.45 ERA with two complete games, 79 saves, 768 strikeouts and a 59-39 record. Davis was a starter for his first three MLB seasons with Tampa Bay and then transitioned mostly to reliever in 2012, his last year as a Ray. That season, he made 54 appearances out of the bullpen, posting a 2.43 ERA in 70.1 innings. After All-Star nods for three straight years (2015-2017) and winning a World Series with the Royals in 2015, Davis established himself as one of the most dominant relievers in the game. item.description: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. Kelly and the Bills made four consecutive Super Bowl appearances while Marino never returned after his lone trip following the 1984 season. These days, the rivalry belongs mostly to Buffalo. Since Josh Allen arrived in Western New York in 2018, he’s gone 14–3 against Miami, including a playoff victory. The Dolphins have managed to sneak in three wins — just enough to make Allen and the rest of Bills Mafia angry before the next meeting. But the Dolphins coming to Buffalo this week look very different from the team that challenged the Bills’ hold on the AFC East just a couple of seasons ago. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle are gone. So are Minkah Fitzpatrick and Bradley Chubb, who now wears a Bills uniform. De’Von Achane is still in Miami but sidelined with an injury. Miami may have a new look, but that doesn’t mean everyone on its sideline is unfamiliar with Buffalo. Despite his quality, the Ecuador international has struggled to establish himself as a regular member of the starting eleven. Given his South American background, a move to either Spanish side could be difficult for him to turn down. That leaves Arsenal facing the prospect of losing an important player, potentially as early as the January transfer window, if they cannot convince him that he has a significant role to play. The club recognised that there was a genuine risk of losing the defender and has acted to strengthen their position. The new agreement is understood to extend his stay beyond 2030, giving Arsenal greater security over his future. item.title: Georgia offensive linemen sign Frontier NIL deal — for their butts?
item.description: Name, image and likeness (NIL) deals have changed the way the country sees college football . Players can make millions of dollars straight out of high school, and their faces are plastered across billboards and cereal boxes as they take the field. But not all NIL deals are quite the same. Juan Gaston and Jahzare Jackson, offensive linemen at the University of Georgia , have signed a major deal with Frontier Airlines as the company launches new first class seats. Frontier says the players are uniquely qualified for the partnership thanks to one distinct feature they both carry — impressive glutes. "Quarterbacks land endorsements for their arms. Receivers land them for their hands. Offensive linemen? Their moment has finally arrived - and they can enjoy it sitting down," Frontier said in a Nov. 19 announcement . UGA players offer 'butt endorsement' Offensive linemen may not have passing stats or sacks under their belts, but they are essential to keeping the quarterback and run game safe. For Georgia, a strong O-line has paid off in their 9-1 season, currently ranked No. 1 in the nation. Gaston and Jackson are part of that success. They stand a combined 13 feet, 5 inches, and weigh a combined 710 pounds, creating a nearly impenetrable wall on the offensive line. Gaston, an Atlanta native, is a sophomore and earned the SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week for Week 11. His father, Juan Gaston Sr., played basketball at Georgia Tech. Jackson, originally from San Diego, is a junior and was a standout basketball player before transitioning to football. He has appeared in 37 games across the 2024, 2025 and 2026 season. "Juan and Jahzare spend every game making room for other people," Frontier CMO Bobby Shroeter said in the announcement. "We thought it was time someone returned the favor." Now signing the contract with their glutes? "I've signed a lot of things, but this was a first," Jackson said. Watch the ad with Georgia football players The partnership was signed in promotion of Frontier's new First Class two-by-two seating, with up to 37 inches of seat pitch. The new seats will be available to passengers beginning March 5, 2027, in addition to premium seating that features extra leg room. The airline will offer a "First Class bundle" that includes one seat, two checked bags, a carry-on and priority boarding. The bundle is on sale now starting at $129 one way, according to Frontier. The powerful *seats* of Jahzare and ⁠Juan Gaston are officially repping Frontier’s new big and comfy First Class seats. ✅ https://t.co/EGwm0YJnm5 — Frontier Airlines (@FlyFrontier) November 19, 2026 Irene Wright is the Atlanta Connect reporter with USA Today’s Deep South Connect team. item.title: Mark Stone Now Golden Knights Career Points Leader
item.description: Boz Bloom-Imagn Images Vegas Golden Knights captain Mark Stone has officially become the franchise’s all-time career points leader . Stone reached the milestone by recording an assist on a goal by Victor Olofsson during the second period of a game on Thursday night against the Dallas Stars. He now has 418 total points for the team, including 147 goals and 271 assists. This total pushes him past former captain Jonathan Marchessault, who finished his time in Vegas with 417 points. The Golden Knights lost the game 4-3 in a shootout , but Stone’s record-breaking moment stands as a major achievement for the 10-year-old franchise. The record comes at a time when the team is struggling with recent losses. Stone entered the matchup with 21 points for the current season and led the squad with 11 goals. He joined the team in a trade from Ottawa during February 2019. His first full season in 2019-20 produced 63 points, starting a streak of four seasons where he posted more than 60 points. Last season, he tied a career high with 73 points. The 34-year-old has shown little sign of slowing down despite his age and the physical toll of the game. Surpassing a Franchise Icon Jonathan Marchessault, who was on the team from the inaugural 2017 season through 2024, held the record for the Golden Knights. During that span, he scored 192 goals and added 225 assists for a total of 417 points. Marchessault was a key part of the team’s Stanley Cup win in 2023, earning the Conn Smythe Trophy as the playoff MVP. He now plays for the Nashville Predators. Stone’s ascent to the top spot highlights his consistency and durability over the last seven years in Las Vegas. The trade that brought him to Vegas in 2019 is now viewed as a foundational move for the franchise’s success. Stone’s path to the record required steady production over many seasons. He has never missed a chance to contribute when healthy. The assist on Thursday night was the final piece needed to pass the mark. It happened just after 7:38 of the second period. Stone’s ability to make the right pass at the right time remains a strength. Fans and analysts see this as a capstone moment for a player who has been the face of the team for a decade. GOLDEN KNIGHTS HISTORY! 🚨 Most regular-season points in Vegas Golden Knights history: Mark Stone: 418 Jonathan Marchessault: 417 Mark Stone is officially the ALL-TIME leading scorer in franchise history! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PL3rddUm7A — Novig (@Novig) November 20, 2026 Recent Struggles and Team Context The game where Stone broke the record did not go as planned for the Golden Knights . The team entered the night having lost their last two games. Dallas led 2-0 early, but the Golden Knights rallied to take a 3-2 lead before Thomas Harley tied it with 3:02 left in regulation. The Stars then won the game 4-3 in the shootout. The loss was the second time these two teams have met this season, with Dallas winning the first meeting 4-3 in overtime. item.title: Why F1 has a decision to make about its greatest asset in a new era for the sport
item.description: On Thursday, in the Colosseum Theatre at Caesars Palace just off Las Vegas ’s iconic strip, the second F1 Business Summit was held. With more than 25 featured speakers across eight sessions and thousands in attendance from dozens of top-brass companies, it is where the bigwig executives coalesce with motorsport’s premier class. And, if recent proclamations are anything to go by, boy, is Sin City the place where deals get announced. A day earlier, F1 announced a high-profile official partnership with popular fitness wearable Whoop, with the next step in broadcasting being the airing of drivers’ heart rates, subject to approval. Naturally, Max Verstappen has already voiced his disapproval . Then, F1 announced an elevation in their partnership with Lego – including an actual Lego race before Saturday’s Grand Prix – and multinational bank Standard Chartered. But it wasn’t until Friday, UK time, when the biggest of the lot arrived in our mailboxes. After 24 years away from the sport, Nike will return to Formula 1 , replacing Puma as the sport’s official apparel and uniform supplier. F1 chief Stefano Domenicali described it as “two of the world’s most iconic brands” uniting, in a period where “Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth”. F1 has announced a new deal with Whoop (PA) F1 has also disclosed a new partnership with Nike (F1) On the commercial front, then, all is very much well. F1 now has more than 35 championship-level partners – 10 of whom are global, top-tier link-ups – and all 11 teams are thriving too. McLaren alone, for instance, have over 55 sponsorship agreements. The valuation of every team is exponentially rising to levels unforeseen when Liberty Media first took over the sport a decade ago. And inevitably, there is no better place to showboat and strut than the bright lights of Vegas. Yet, given what has been a largely forgettable season on-track, that is just as well. Ahead of this weekend’s 21st round, both championships are wrapped up: Mercedes clinched their first constructors’ title in five years at the last race in Brazil, while 20-year-old Kimi Antonelli became the sport’s youngest-ever champion a race earlier in Mexico. The whole year, however, has been overshadowed by justified complaints about the new era of engine and chassis regulations, which have been slated from just about every corner. From the first qualifying session in March in Australia, concerns were awash in the paddock. Slowing down at the end of straights to go quicker – such were the requirements to recharge the battery – is clearly not what F1 should be about. And provisional plans are now already in place to reintroduce V8 engines from 2030. It is a clear admission: they got it wrong. And the last week or so has seen another controversy rear its ugly head. A seasoned British journalist from the Daily Mail has had his accreditation revoked for the final three races of the year after calling Charles Leclerc a “sneaky little bastard” in an article

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes role and plans to revamp Man United philosophy
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino hopes to transform Manchester United ’s style of play after inheriting a team with among the poorest running statistics in the Premier League this season. The Argentine coach called for “context” surrounding data, despite United currently second to last in terms of distance covered this season, with physicality consistently tied to the way the former Spurs and Chelsea manager’s teams have played. Yet Pochettino, ahead of Sunday’s first game against Liverpool at Anfield, has vowed to “create something from scratch” after inheriting a United side inside the relegation zone. “We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, our own ideas and philosophy, in the way we like to work, we find supportive people in the club, that make it easy, the adaptation, at the same time, we need to improve the players, to create the way to find a way to perform,” Pochettino said. “We are not focused on culture, it’s a massive work, you need to spend 10 years to focus on culture, it’s clear, a historic club. "When we arrive, we found a group of players that we propose to do the football that we feel, being brave, be Man United, you know? It's about proposing the idea, they buy that idea, to be brave and try take that to the field. It's a debate that I don't like to go in, we cannot talk about things without context. “On the data without context, it's easy to manipulate the data, I need to be honest, sometimes the data can show some things. We'll try improve the data and numbers in every single area of the field. We are here, not to denounce things, we're here to build things, perform and win games. Mauricio Pochettino is in charge for Man United at Liverpool on Sunday (Reuters) And Pochettino also confirmed Bruno Fernandes will remain his captain. “All the players, we were chatting, it was amazing from day one, Bruno is our captain, an important player,” Pochettino confirmed. “But all the players need to think they are important, from the bottom to the top. “I spent three hours, chatting in my office, with all the players, maybe I miss some injured players. In the next few days, we will talk in an individual way with all of them. It’s important to listen to what they need to say, understand the place they are. Not only on the field, off the field, what’s going on. Some conversations, some collective way, meetings, but focus is on Sunday.”

What’s more, he did not train today. He may not be available for the match against Villarreal this weekend. The defender has struggled with injuries for years now, though he has generally played well when available. His fitness issues are one reason why Barça are said to be scouring the market for another center-back. Christensen missed a photoshoot with Barça Licensing & Merchandising because he was under the team doctor’s care. The Catalans have Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín as starters but no other recognized senior center-backs apart from Christensen after letting Ronald Araujo go to Liverpool FC. Typically, teams carry four senior center-backs. Cubarsí himself has recently returned from injury. Signs point to him being available for the Villarreal match, but if he is not ready, Barcelona will have to shuffle players around. Eric Garcia, who started out as a center-back but has played as a full-back more recently, would be a prime candidate. Jules Koundé is a similar case, a former center-back turned full-back, though he is also just back from injury. And then there’s Frenkie de Jong, a midfielder who has been deployed in multiple positions, including as a central defender. The club has yet to confirm Christensen’s injury, and the exact diagnosis is unknown at the time. It’s not yet known how long he will be out. item.title: Maverick Vinales withdraws from the Portuguese GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Maverick Vinales will sit out the remainder of MotoGP's Portuguese Grand Prix weekend, with Tech3 drafting in KTM's test rider Pol Espargaro as his replacement. Vinales has been struggling with discomfort since he dislocated his left shoulder more than a year ago at the 2025 German GP. The injury forced him to stop on three occasions, including just before the summer break, when the team even considered dropping him entirely from its line-up. The Spaniard returned to action in Japan, but a busy second half of the season has left him in a state of fatigue, prompting him to withdraw from Portimao after FP1. "Following a medical assessment carried out after the first free practice session (FP1), Maverick has decided, together with his team and KTM, to withdraw from the Portuguese Grand Prix," Tech3 explained in a statement. "He will be replaced by Pol Espargaro for the rest of the weekend. "The Spanish rider will continue to assess his condition ahead of his home race and the final round of the 2026 MotoGP season, which will take place in Valencia. Further information will be provided in due course." Maverick Vinales, Red Bull KTM Tech 3 Maverick Vinales, Red Bull KTM Tech 3 Next week's Valencia round could mark Vinales' last race in the world championship after 16 years of participation, as he has no contract for 2027. He has achieved a total of 26 grand prix wins across all three categories, including 10 during his 11-year stint in the premier class. "I have worked very hard over the last month to get back to my best level and be ready to race again," the rider said. "Unfortunately, this circuit makes it very difficult to control the bike; on top of that, I have felt pain in my shoulder. "It has been a very difficult decision, because I want to keep pushing, but we have concluded that the best thing is to stop. The important thing is to prevent further damage to the shoulder and avoid dangerous situations on track; I will remain focused on my recovery. It is disappointing, especially after all the work I have done to come back, but I have to listen to my body," the Spanish rider added. Espargaro, who had already replaced Vinales in as many as four races this season, will once again put on his Tech3 leathers to take to the track this afternoon in the Practice session. His best result came at Silverstone, where he crossed the finish line in 13th place. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. item.title: NWSL’s early kickoff times for the quarterfinals harm the game: ‘It’s getting old’
item.description: The trouble with having a glass-half-full mentality is that it can obscure a legitimate invitation to be frustrated. Enter the early morning kickoff. A 9 a.m. start time for Pacific Coast time zone dwellers? All the more reason to jumpstart the day. Take that 7:30 a.m. workout class, toss in a load of laundry just before the lineups are announced, maybe whip up a nice breakfast for the occasion. Make it productive, so that it feels as though a postseason draw pulled so far away from prime time actually worked out in your favor. This would have been an understandable response before the league signed its landmark $240 million media rights deal in 2023 , and it was still an acceptable one in the context of a one-off regular season match. Who doesn’t love the occasional brunch game? But as the NWSL enters its 14th postseason on Friday, Nov. 6 in San Diego, concluding on Sunday in D.C., fans are once again presented a glass containing some inadequate portion and asked to supplant its emptiness with resolution. Playoffs are meant to be glorious crescendos to the season. They are also massive opportunities to grow an audience. It’s difficult to do that when games are scheduled at inconvenient times that require intentional planning. If anything, these early starts echo broader calls for NWSL clubs to own their own venues, which would address a significant part of the problem. The other part rests with the status quo of sports itself. The pace of women’s sports’ growth is what makes it such a thrilling venture to be a part of, but it has outgrown the implication that putting a game on cable television is an accomplishment in itself. It’s getting old Two of the four NWSL quarterfinals this year — Kansas City Current vs. Angel City FC and Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign — have morning start times for those in the Pacific and Mountain time zones. And only one match can be considered scheduled for a prime time slot when the San Diego Wave host the Utah Royals on Friday at 10 p.m. ET/7 p.m. PT on Prime Video. The following day the Current host Angel City at noon ET/9 a.m. PT on CBS. On Sunday, NWSL Shield winners Gotham kick off a double-header on ABC when they host the eighth-ranked Seattle Reign at 12:30 p.m. ET/9:30 a.m. before the Spirit’s 3 p.m. ET/noon PT matchup against the Portland Thorns at Audi Field. Apart from the start times, the lopsidedness of this playoff schedule — one match on Friday and Saturday, and two on Sunday — also creates a wider chasm of potential competitive advantage among the teams. The winner of San Diego vs. Utah, for example, will not know their next opponent until about 48 hours after their game concludes. If the Royals upset the Wave, their semifinal fixture would require travel to either D.C. or Portland. The spread of matches next weekend is partly due to conflicts with other tenants in the stadiums NWSL teams occupy.
